title: Locally principal inverse-image complements and supported module kernels
statement: Let $Y,T$ be schemes [def-pc-scheme], let $q:Y\to T$ be a morphism, and let $E\hookrightarrow T$ be a locally principal closed subscheme [def-weil-closed-immersion], meaning that its ideal is generated by one function on a neighbourhood of every point. Put $D=q^{-1}(E)=Y\times_TE$, the inverse-image closed subscheme [def-pc-fibre-product], and $j:V=Y\setminus D\hookrightarrow Y$ [def-weil-open-immersion]. Let $H$ be a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_Y$-module [pqf-def-coherent]. Define the subsheaf $K\subseteq H$ by $K(W)=\{s\in H(W):s|_{W\cap V}=0\}$ for every open $W\subseteq Y$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Then $D$ is locally principal, $j$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated [def-weil-finite-type-morphism, def-weil-quasi-separated-morphism], and $K$ is quasi-coherent. Moreover, $K=\ker(H\to j_*(H|_V))$ sectionwise, for the module pushforward $j_*$ [def-pc-module-pullback], and its sections are precisely the sections of $H$ whose germs vanish at every point outside $D$. No flatness of $q$ or nonzerodivisor condition on a local equation of $D$ is assumed.

proof.text: Let $\mathcal I_E$ be the ideal of $E$. The closed-subscheme base-change lemma identifies the ideal of $D$ with $\operatorname{Im}(q^*\mathcal I_E\to\mathcal O_Y)$. Fix $y\in Y$ and choose an open neighbourhood $U$ of $q(y)$ where $\mathcal I_E=(f)$. By the affine-open basis lemma choose an affine neighbourhood $W=\operatorname{Spec}B\subseteq q^{-1}U$ of $y$; put $b=q^\sharp(f)|_W$. In the tensor description of $q^*$, every local tensor $a\otimes cf$ maps to $acb$, and $1\otimes f$ maps to $b$. Thus the image ideal on $W$ is exactly $(b)$ and $D$ is locally principal. This calculation uses the image of the pulled-back ideal, not injectivity of its map to $\mathcal O_Y$; it remains valid for $b=0$ and for zero divisors.

source.place: Tag 053P, lemma-pullback-locally-principal (omitted proof expanded using Schemes Tag 01JU, lemma-fibre-product-immersion).

proof.text: The neighbourhoods $W=\operatorname{Spec}B$ from Step 1 cover $Y$, and $W\cap V=D(b)$. The localization homeomorphism and quasi-compactness of spectra make every $D(c)\subseteq\operatorname{Spec}B$ quasi-compact. If $A\subseteq W$ is any affine open, the basic-open basis gives a cover $A=\bigcup_iD(c_i)$ with $D(c_i)\subseteq A$; quasi-compactness of $A$ gives a finite subcover. Then $A\cap D(b)=\bigcup_iD(bc_i)$ is quasi-compact. Hence $D(b)\hookrightarrow W$ is quasi-compact by the definition, and locality on the target gives quasi-compactness of $j$. In particular $V$ meets every affine open of $Y$ in a quasi-compact open, so $V$ is retrocompact.

proof.text: Since $j$ is an open immersion it is a monomorphism, hence separated by the scheme-monomorphism lemma, and therefore quasi-separated by the separated-implies-quasi-separated lemma. These statements are relative to $Y$ and do not require $Y$ to be quasi-separated.

proof.text: Unpack ordinary module pushforward for this open inclusion: $(j_*G)(W)=G(W\cap V)$, with $\mathcal O_Y(W)$ acting by restriction to $W\cap V$. This is a sheaf by gluing on the intersections with $V$. Taking $G=H|_V$, the restriction maps define an $\mathcal O_Y$-linear morphism $H\to j_*(H|_V)$. Kernels of module sheaves are sectionwise, so its kernel on $W$ is exactly $K(W)$ as defined in the statement. Equivalently the sheaf gluing axiom directly shows that these submodules form a subsheaf: restrictions preserve vanishing, and sections vanishing on the intersections of a cover with $V$ glue to a section vanishing on $W\cap V$.

source.place: Tag 07ZP, lemma-sections-supported-on-closed-subset, proof of (3), its sectionwise exact sequence; Sheaves Tag 0095, definition-pushforward; Modules Tag 01AH, lemma-limits-colimits.

proof.text: Apply the supported-sections theorem to the scheme $Y$, the closed subset $|D|$, and the quasi-coherent module $H$. Step 2 verifies exactly its retrocompact-complement hypothesis. Its subsheaf on an open $W$ is $\{s\in H(W):s|_{W\setminus|D|}=0\}$, which equals $K(W)$ since $W\setminus|D|=W\cap V$. The theorem therefore gives that $K$ is quasi-coherent.

Finally, if $s|_{W\cap V}=0$, its germ at every point of $W\cap V$ is zero. Conversely a zero germ at $x\in W\cap V$ means that $s$ is zero on some open neighbourhood of $x$ in $W\cap V$. These neighbourhoods cover $W\cap V$; the uniqueness part of the sheaf axiom makes $s|_{W\cap V}=0$. Thus $K(W)$ is precisely the set of sections with all germs outside $D$ zero, as asserted.

Step 3: open immersion => monomorphism => separated => quasi-separated, all relative statements. Step 4: the kernel is computed sectionwise, (j_*G)(W)=G(W∩V), so it equals K. Step 5: lem-trf-supported-sections-quasi-coherent is applied through its statement, with Z=|D| closed and the retrocompactness from Step 2. Step 6: germs and sheaf uniqueness.
